Role of Data in Making Better Decisions
Data doesn't make decisions. It makes decisions better.
01
Reduces uncertainty
Replaces opinion with evidence
EXAMPLE
Which paint shade sells in which district next month
02
Reveals what we can't see
Patterns across millions of transactions
EXAMPLE
Which loan customers will accept a second product
03
Speeds up feedback
Tells us quickly if a decision is working
EXAMPLE
A/B testing a price or a homepage
04
Makes decisions repeatable
Turns one expert's judgment into a system
EXAMPLE
Credit scoring instead of a branch manager's gut

Why More Data Can Make Decisions Worse
Four traps to watch for
TRAP 01
$12.9M
Garbage in, garbage out
Average yearly cost of poor data quality to an organisation
Gartner
TRAP 02
~2×
Signal vs noise
Google Flu Trends predicted roughly double the actual doctor visits
Search-query big data, 2011–13
TRAP 03
70%
Analysis paralysis
Decide with ~70% of the information you wish you had. Waiting for 90% is too slow.
Jeff Bezos
TRAP 04
Confirmation bias with a spreadsheet
Data used to justify a decision already made
4
The Analytics Continuum
From hindsight to foresight
HINDSIGHT
Descriptive
What happened?
Sales dashboard: Pune sales fell 12% last month
INSIGHT
Diagnostic
Why did it happen?
Drill-down: the fall is only in exterior emulsions, only in rain-hit districts
FORESIGHT
Predictive
What will happen?
Model forecasts next month's demand by shade, pack size & pin code
ACTION
Prescriptive
What should we do?
Optimiser decides how much stock to send to each dealer, and when
EMERGING
AUTOMATION
Autonomous / Agentic
Can the system act on its own?
AI agent reorders stock and adjusts dealer offers within guard-rails
Most organisations are still using AI mainly to understand what happened faster, not to anticipate what happens next.
Value ↑ and difficulty ↑ as you climb · Gartner Analytic Ascendancy Model (2012)

Four Inputs to Every Decision
Intuition, Research, Analysis, AI/ML: four voices at the table
Intuition
Research
Analysis
AI / ML
WHAT IT IS
Pattern recognition from experience
EXAMPLE
A founder sensing a new category
WHAT IT IS
Asking & observing people: surveys, interviews, field visits, experiments
EXAMPLE
Field study of how rural women buy paint
WHAT IT IS
Structured examination of existing data: stats, BI, modelling
EXAMPLE
Diagnosing a sales drop by region
WHAT IT IS
Algorithms that learn patterns from large data and predict or act at scale
EXAMPLE
Bajaj Finance's AI generating loan offers from call recordings

Stable & repeatable?
LOW DATA
HIGH DATA

How much reliable data exists?
Intuition + small experiments
→ learn fast
e.g. entering a new category
Research + expert rules
→ build the data
e.g. a new loan product in a new region
Analysis informs
→ leaders decide
e.g. responding to a new competitor with ₹10,000 cr
AI/ML automates
→ human monitors
e.g. credit scoring, delivery ETAs, demand forecasts
SECOND RULE: REVERSIBILITY
One-way vs two-way doors
Jeff Bezos
Two-way door
Reversible, cheap
Decide fast. Let data, AI and small tests guide.
One-way door
Irreversible, costly
Slow down. Triangulate all four inputs.

Suggested Decision Framework
Who owns which decision
DECISION LAYER
WHO LEADS
ROLE OF THE OTHER
Strategic
What to create, which market, whom to acquire
Human judgment
Data informs, challenges and stress-tests
Tactical
Pricing, campaigns, assortment
Analysis + experiments
Intuition generates hypotheses to test
Operational
What to recommend, what to stock, whom to call
AI / ML
Humans set guard-rails, audit for bias & drift
11
Five
rules for better decisions
01
Start with the decision, not the data
Define the question first (CRISP-DM: Business Understanding, covered next session)
02
Quality beats quantity
Bad data at scale is just faster mistakes
03
Climb the continuum step by step
Descriptive → diagnostic → predictive → prescriptive
04
Match the tool to the decision
Repeatable + data-rich → AI. Novel + irreversible → informed judgment.
05
Analytics is a multiplier, not a moat
It wins when tied to proprietary data, execution and a business model. Bajaj Finance could do this because it had data on crores of customers.
